**RE: Member appeal — denial of prior authorization for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)**
**Member:** Jordan Foster
**Member ID:** W794852405
**Reference number:** POC-EE22487639-86426
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-07
**Governing policy:** Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf (Date of Last Revision: 04/25)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-07 states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file document the conservative care the plan's own policy describes.

I am citing the plan's policy, **Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)**, and only that policy, below.

### What the plan's policy says, and what my records show

**1. Age and diagnosis.** The policy states:

> "A. Age ≥ 18 years; B. Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc;"

I am [age] years old (date of birth [DOB]). My MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-28 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis.

**2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging.** The policy states:

> "C. Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

The same MRI of 2026-06-28 documents compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is imaging-confirmed nerve root compression, which is the threshold requirement in this section of the plan's policy.

**3. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit and failure of conservative therapy.** The policy states:

> "2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

My records document radicular pain into my right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. My symptoms have lasted 12 months and are described in the records as progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.

The policy then lists what conservative therapy must include. On physical therapy, it states:

> "a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or doc umentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

My records document supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, for 10 weeks, from 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, with 16 visits completed. This is recorded in my physical therapy discharge note. Ten weeks of completed, supervised therapy is more than double the four weeks the plan's own policy sets out.

On activity modification and medication, the policy states:

> "b. ≥ four weeks activity modification; c. One of the following:"

and, as one of the listed options:

> "i. NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

with the alternative option being:

> "ii. Epidural steroid injection."

My records document **NSAIDs taken for 6 months with inadequate relief** — well beyond the three weeks the policy requires — and a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09**, which gave only about three weeks of partial relief. My records therefore document both of the alternatives in this part of the policy, where the policy asks for only one.

On activity modification, my records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and that my pain is unrelieved by rest. If the plan requires separate documentation of a prescribed period of activity modification, I am requesting that it identify that in writing, and I am asking my treating providers to supply the supporting note. Records of activity modification from [date] to [date] are enclosed, if available: [describe or mark "not available"].

### What I am asking the plan to clarify

Several of the criteria quoted above end in a colon and introduce further sub-lists that were not included in the excerpts available to me. I am not attempting to restate parts of the policy I have not seen, and I am not quoting any requirement — any duration, count, grade, or threshold — that does not appear in the language above. **Where the policy lists further conditions that I have not reproduced here, I am asking the plan to identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria it applied to reach this denial, and which document in my file it found insufficient.** The notice I received states a general conclusion about conservative treatment but does not identify which policy element was not met.

The plan's policy also contains a separate pathway based on motor deficit, which states:

> "1. R adiculopathy with motor deficit and one of the following: a. Severe weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by: a score of ≤ 3 on the Me dical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale, or the inability to ambulate;"

and

> "b. Mild to moderate weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by a score of 4 on the Medical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale and one of the following:"

> "i. Worsening weakness or motor deficit; ii. Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following:"

My records describe a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level but do not state a numeric Medical Research Council muscle strength score. If the plan reviewed my request under this pathway, I ask that it say so, and I ask that my treating surgeon be given the opportunity to supply the graded strength examination. In any event, the conservative care listed in that pathway — including:

> "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

> "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification; c) One of the following:"

> "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; 2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

— matches the care already documented in my file: 10 weeks and 16 visits of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09. All of this occurred within the last year.

### My request

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and my records document the imaging-confirmed nerve root compression, the radicular symptoms, and the completed course of conservative treatment described in the plan's own policy. I respectfully ask the plan to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 (reference POC-EE22487639-86426) and authorize CPT 63030; or
2. If the denial is maintained, provide me with a written statement identifying the exact criterion in Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114) that my records did not meet, the specific records reviewed, and the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the decision.

Per my denial notice, this appeal must be received by **2027-02-03** (180 days from the date of the notice). I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file through ambetterhealth.com by selecting North Carolina and using that state's appeal/grievance form, or by calling the number on my ID card.

Please also treat this letter as a request for a copy of all documents, records, and criteria the plan relied on in making this determination.

**Enclosures:** [MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-06-28]; [physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, 16 visits]; [injection record dated 2026-06-09]; [medication history]; [office notes from Dr. Reyes, MD]; [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-07]

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

_____________________________
Jordan Foster
Member ID: W794852405
Date of birth: [DOB]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]
Address: [Street Address, City, NC ZIP]
